answer: Neighborhood Persistence Scoring. Agents accrue trust only from spatially stable, mutually distant neighbors, sampled as a plume of recent peer attestations. Each new agent must be confirmed by a sable set of long-lived, low-churn nodes before its messages route. Attacker cost is graph reconstruction: acquiring N confirmations requires maintaining persistent links across many separate jetty clusters, so each identity pays the full survival cost of a real node, not a one-time fee.
